problem:
Title: Characterization of Natural Transformation Between Bifunctors

Let $\mathbf C, \mathbf D$ and $\mathbf E$ be [[Definition:Category|categories]].

Let $F, G : \mathbf C \times \mathbf D \to \mathbf E$ be [[Definition:Bifunctor|bifunctors]] from the [[Definition:Product Category|product category]] $\mathbf C \times \mathbf D$ to the [[Definition:Category|category]] $\mathbf E$.

For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]] $C \in\mathbf C$ let: 
:$F \tuple{C, -}$ and $G \tuple{C, -}$
denote the [[Definition:Functor|functors]] obtained by [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the first variable]] of $F$ and $G$, respectively, with $C$.

For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]] $D \in\mathbf D$ let:
:$F \tuple{-, D}$ and $G \tuple{-, D}$
denote the [[Definition:Functor|functors]] obtained by [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the second variable]] of $F$ and $G$, respectively, with $D$.

For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]] $\tuple{C, D} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D$ let:
:$\alpha_{\tuple{C, D}} : F \tuple{C,D} \to G \tuple{C,D}$ 
denote a [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphism]] in $\mathbf E$.

Then:
:$\alpha : F \to G$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
{{iff}}
:$(1)\quad$ For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $C \in \mathbf C : \alpha \tuple{C, -} : F \tuple{C, -} \to G \tuple{C, -}$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
:$(2)\quad$ For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $D \in \mathbf D : \alpha \tuple{-, D} : F \tuple{-, D} \to G \tuple{-, D}$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]

where:
:for [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|objects]] $C \in \mathbf C$ and $D \in \mathbf D$, $\alpha \tuple{C, -}_D = \alpha_{\tuple{C, D}}$
and:
:for [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|objects]] $C \in \mathbf C$ and $D \in \mathbf D$, $\alpha \tuple{-, D}_C = \alpha_{\tuple{C, D}}$

0001 | == Proof 1 ==
0002 | === [[Characterization of Natural Transformation Between Bifunctors/Proof 1 Necessary Condition|Necessary Condition]] ===
0003 | 
0004 | Let $\alpha : F \to G$ be a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]].
0005 | 
0006 | By definition of [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]:
0007 | :for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $f: C \to C' \in \mathbf C$ and $g: D \to D' \in \mathbf D$ the following [[Definition:Commutative Diagram|diagrams commute]]:
0008 | 
0009 | ::<nowiki>$\begin{xy}
0010 | <0em,0em>*+{\map F {C, D} } = "FCD",
0011 | <12em,0em>*+{\map F {C', D} } = "FC2D",
0012 | <0em,-6em>*+{\map G {C, D} } = "GCD",
0013 | <12em,-6em>*+{\map G {C', D} } = "GC2D",
0014 | 
0015 | "FCD";"FC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_1em/{\map F {f, \operatorname{id}_D} },
0016 | "GCD";"GC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^1em/{\map G {f, \operatorname{id}_D} },
0017 | "FCD";"GCD" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^2em/{\alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } },
0018 | "FC2D";"GC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_2em/{\alpha_{\tuple{C', D} } },
0019 | 
0020 | <0em,-12em>*+{\map F {C, D} } = "FCD",
0021 | <12em,-12em>*+{\map F {C, D'} } = "FCD2",
0022 | <0em,-18em>*+{\map G {C, D} } = "GCD",
0023 | <12em,-18em>*+{\map G {C, D'} } = "GCD2",
0024 | 
0025 | "FCD";"FCD2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_1em/{\map F {\operatorname{id}_C, g} },
0026 | "GCD";"GCD2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^1em/{\map G {\operatorname{id}_C, g} },
0027 | "FCD";"GCD" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^2em/{\alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } },
0028 | "FCD2";"GCD2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_2em/{\alpha_{\tuple{C, D'} } },
0029 | \end{xy}$</nowiki>
0030 | 
0031 | That is:
0032 | :for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $f: C \to C' \in \mathbf C$ and $g: D \to D' \in \mathbf D$ the following [[Definition:Commutative Diagram|diagrams commute]]:
0033 | 
0034 | ::<nowiki>$\begin{xy}
0035 | <0em,0em>*+{\map {F \tuple{-, D} } C} = "FCD",
0036 | <15em,0em>*+{\map {F \tuple{-, D} } {C'} } = "FC2D",
0037 | <0em,-6em>*+{\map {G \tuple{-, D} } C} = "GCD",
0038 | <15em,-6em>*+{\map {G \tuple{-, D} } {C'} } = "GC2D",
0039 | 
0040 | "FCD";"FC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_1em/{\map {F \tuple{-, D} } f },
0041 | "GCD";"GC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^1em/{\map {F \tuple{-, D} } f },
0042 | "FCD";"GCD" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^3em/{\alpha \tuple{-, D}_C },
0043 | "FC2D";"GC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_3em/{\alpha \tuple{-, D}_{C'} },
0044 | 
0045 | <0em,-12em>*+{\map {F \tuple{C, -} } D} = "FCD",
0046 | <15em,-12em>*+{\map {F \tuple{C, -} } {D'} } = "FCD2",
0047 | <0em,-18em>*+{\map {G \tuple{C, -} } D} = "GCD",
0048 | <15em,-18em>*+{\map {G \tuple{C, -} } {D'} } = "GCD2",
0049 | 
0050 | "FCD";"FCD2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_1em/{\map {F \tuple{C, -} } g},
0051 | "GCD";"GCD2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^1em/{\map {G \tuple{C, -} } g},
0052 | "FCD";"GCD" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^3em/{\alpha \tuple{C, -}_D },
0053 | "FCD2";"GCD2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_3em/{\alpha \tuple{C, -}_{D'} },
0054 | \end{xy}$</nowiki>
0055 | by definitions of 
0056 | :* [[Definition:Functor|functors]] obtained by [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the first variable]] and [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the second variable]]
0057 | :* $\alpha \tuple{C, -}$ and $\alpha \tuple{-, D}$
0058 | 
0059 | It follows that:
0060 | :* For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $C \in \mathbf C : \alpha \tuple{C, -} : F \tuple{C, -} \to G \tuple{C, -}$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
0061 | :* For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $D \in \mathbf D : \alpha \tuple{-, D} : F \tuple{-, D} \to G \tuple{-, D}$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
0062 | by definition.{{qed|lemma}}

0064 | === [[Characterization of Natural Transformation Between Bifunctors/Proof 1 Sufficient Condition|Sufficient Condition]] ===
0065 | 
0066 | Let:
0067 | :$(1)\quad$ For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $C \in \mathbf C : \alpha \tuple{C, -} : F \tuple{C, -} \to G \tuple{C, -}$ be a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
0068 | :$(2)\quad$ For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $D \in \mathbf D : \alpha \tuple{-, D} : F \tuple{-, D} \to G \tuple{-, D}$ be a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
0069 | 
0070 | By definition of [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]:
0071 | :for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $f: C \to C' \in \mathbf C$ and $g: D \to D' \in \mathbf D$ the following [[Definition:Commutative Diagram|diagrams commute]]:
0072 | 
0073 | ::<nowiki>$\begin{xy}
0074 | <0em,0em>*+{\map {F \tuple{-, D} } C} = "FCD",
0075 | <15em,0em>*+{\map {F \tuple{-, D} } {C'} } = "FC2D",
0076 | <0em,-6em>*+{\map {G \tuple{-, D} } C} = "GCD",
0077 | <15em,-6em>*+{\map {G \tuple{-, D} } {C'} } = "GC2D",
0078 | 
0079 | "FCD";"FC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_1em/{\map {F \tuple{-, D} } f },
0080 | "GCD";"GC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^1em/{\map {F \tuple{-, D} } f },
0081 | "FCD";"GCD" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^3em/{\alpha \tuple{-, D}_C },
0082 | "FC2D";"GC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_3em/{\alpha \tuple{-, D}_{C'} },
0083 | 
0084 | <0em,-12em>*+{\map {F \tuple{C', -} } D} = "FC2D",
0085 | <15em,-12em>*+{\map {F \tuple{C', -} } {D'} } = "FC2D2",
0086 | <0em,-18em>*+{\map {G \tuple{C', -} } D} = "GC2D",
0087 | <15em,-18em>*+{\map {G \tuple{C', -} } {D'} } = "GC2D2",
0088 | 
0089 | "FC2D";"FC2D2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_1em/{\map {F \tuple{C', -} } g},
0090 | "GC2D";"GC2D2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^1em/{\map {G \tuple{C', -} } g},
0091 | "FC2D";"GC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^3em/{\alpha \tuple{C', -}_D },
0092 | "FC2D2";"GC2D2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_3em/{\alpha \tuple{C', -}_{D'} },
0093 | \end{xy}$</nowiki>
0094 | 
0095 | That is:
0096 | :for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $\tuple{f: C \to C', g: D \to D'} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D$ the following [[Definition:Commutative Diagram|diagram commutes]]:
0097 | 
0098 | ::<nowiki>$\begin{xy}
0099 | <0em,0em>*+{\map F {C, D} } = "FCD",
0100 | <12em,0em>*+{\map F {C', D} } = "FC2D",
0101 | <24em,0em>*+{\map F {C', D'} } = "FC2D2",
0102 | <0em,-6em>*+{\map G {C, D} } = "GCD",
0103 | <12em,-6em>*+{\map G {C', D} } = "GC2D",
0104 | <24em,-6em>*+{\map G {C', D'} } = "GC2D2",
0105 | 
0106 | "FCD";"FC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_1em/{\map F {f, \operatorname{id}_D} },
0107 | "GCD";"GC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^1em/{\map G {f, \operatorname{id}_D} },
0108 | "FCD";"GCD" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^2em/{\alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } },
0109 | "FC2D";"GC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_2em/{\alpha_{\tuple{C', D} } },
0110 | "FC2D";"FC2D2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_1em/{\map F {\operatorname{id}_{C'}, g} },
0111 | "GC2D";"GC2D2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^1em/{\map G {\operatorname{id}_{C'}, g} },
0112 | "FC2D2";"GC2D2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_2em/{\alpha_{\tuple{C', D'} } },
0113 | \end{xy}$</nowiki>
0114 | by definitions of 
0115 | :* [[Definition:Functor|functors]] obtained by [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the first variable]] and [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the second variable]]
0116 | :* $\alpha \tuple{C, -}$ and $\alpha \tuple{-, D}$
0117 | 
0118 | By definition of [[Definition:Bifunctor|bifunctor]] and [[Definition:Identity Morphism|identity morphism]]:
0119 | :for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $\tuple{f: C \to C', g: D \to D'} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D$ the following [[Definition:Commutative Diagram|diagram commutes]]:
0120 | 
0121 | ::<nowiki>$\begin{xy}
0122 | <0em,4em>*+{\map F {C, D} } = "FCD",
0123 | <12em,0em>*+{\map F {C', D} } = "FC2D",
0124 | <24em,4em>*+{\map F {C', D'} } = "FC2D2",
0125 | <0em,-10em>*+{\map G {C, D} } = "GCD",
0126 | <12em,-6em>*+{\map G {C', D} } = "GC2D",
0127 | <24em,-10em>*+{\map G {C', D'} } = "GC2D2",
0128 | 
0129 | "FCD";"FC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^1.5em/{\map F {f, \operatorname{id}_D} },
0130 | "GCD";"GC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_1.5em/{\map G {f, \operatorname{id}_D} },
0131 | "FCD";"GCD" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^2em/{\alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } },
0132 | "FC2D";"GC2D" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_2em/{\alpha_{\tuple{C', D} } },
0133 | "FC2D";"FC2D2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^1.5em/{\map F {\operatorname{id}_{C'}, g} },
0134 | "GC2D";"GC2D2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_1.5em/{\map G {\operatorname{id}_{C'}, g} },
0135 | "FC2D2";"GC2D2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_2em/{\alpha_{\tuple{C', D'} } },
0136 | "FCD";"FC2D2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/_1em/{\map F {f,g} },
0137 | "GCD";"GC2D2" **@{-} ?>*@{>} ?<>(.5)*!/^1em/{\map G {f,g} },
0138 | \end{xy}$</nowiki>
0139 | 
0140 | It follows that $\alpha : F \to G$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]] by definition.{{qed}}

0142 | == Proof 2 ==
0143 | === [[Characterization of Natural Transformation Between Bifunctors/Proof 2 Necessary Condition|Necessary Condition]] ===
0144 | 
0145 | Let $\alpha : F \to G$ be a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]].
0146 | 
0147 | By definition of [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]:
0148 | :for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $\tuple{f: C \to C', g:D \to D'} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D : \map G {f, g} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } = \alpha_{\tuple{C', D'} } \circ \map F {f, g}$
0149 | 
0150 | In particular:
0151 | :$(3)\quad$ for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $\tuple{f: C \to C', \operatorname{id}_D:D \to D} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D : \map G {f, \operatorname{id}_D} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } = \alpha_{\tuple{C', D} } \circ \map F {f, \operatorname{id}_D}$
0152 | and:
0153 | :$(4)\quad$ for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $\tuple{\operatorname{id}_C: C \to C, g:D \to D'} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D : \map G {\operatorname{id}_C, g} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } = \alpha_{\tuple{C, D'} } \circ \map F {\operatorname{id}_C, g}$
0154 | 
0155 | For all [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]] $D \in \mathbf D$ and [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $f: C \to C' \in \mathbf C$, we have:
0156 | {{begin-eqn}}
0157 | {{eqn | l = \map {G \tuple{-, D} } f \circ \alpha \tuple{-, D}_C
0158 |       | r = \map G {f, \operatorname{id}_D} \circ \alpha \tuple{-, D}_C
0159 |       | c = {{Defof|Bifunctor|substitution of second variable}}
0160 | }}
0161 | {{eqn | r = \map G {f, \operatorname{id}_D} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} }
0162 |       | c = Definition of $\alpha \tuple{-, D}$
0163 | }}
0164 | {{eqn | r = \alpha_{\tuple{C', D} } \circ \map F {f, \operatorname{id}_D}
0165 |       | c = By $(3)$
0166 | }}
0167 | {{eqn | r = \alpha \tuple{-, D}_{C'} \circ \map F {f, \operatorname{id}_D}
0168 |       | c = Definition of $\alpha \tuple{-, D}$
0169 | }}
0170 | {{eqn | r = \alpha \tuple{-, D}_{C'} \circ \map {F \tuple{-, D} } f
0171 |       | c = {{Defof|Bifunctor|substitution of second variable}}
0172 | }}
0173 | {{end-eqn}}
0174 | 
0175 | It follows that for each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $D \in \mathbf D$:
0176 | :$\alpha \tuple{-, D} : F \tuple{-, D} \to G \tuple{-, D}$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
0177 | by definition.
0178 | 
0179 | For all [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]] $C \in \mathbf C$ and [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $g: D \to D' \in \mathbf D$, we have:
0180 | {{begin-eqn}}
0181 | {{eqn | l = \map {G \tuple{C, -} } f \circ \alpha \tuple{C, -}_D
0182 |       | r = \map G {\operatorname{id}_C, g} \circ \alpha \tuple{C, -}_D
0183 |       | c = {{Defof|Bifunctor|substitution of first variable}}
0184 | }}
0185 | {{eqn | r = \map G {\operatorname{id}_C, g} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} }
0186 |       | c = Definition of $\alpha \tuple{C, -}$
0187 | }}
0188 | {{eqn | r = \alpha_{\tuple{C, D'} } \circ \map F {\operatorname{id}_C, g}
0189 |       | c = By $(4)$
0190 | }}
0191 | {{eqn | r = \alpha \tuple{C, -}_{D'} \circ \map F {\operatorname{id}_C, g}
0192 |       | c = Definition of $\alpha \tuple{C, -}$
0193 | }}
0194 | {{eqn | r = \alpha \tuple{C, -}_{D'} \circ \map {F \tuple{C, -} } g
0195 |       | c = {{Defof|Bifunctor|substitution of first variable}}
0196 | }}
0197 | {{end-eqn}}
0198 | 
0199 | It follows that for each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $C \in \mathbf C$:
0200 | :$\alpha \tuple{C, -} : F \tuple{C, -} \to G \tuple{C, -}$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
0201 | by definition.
0202 | 
0203 | The result follows.{{qed|lemma}}

0205 | === [[Characterization of Natural Transformation Between Bifunctors/Proof 2 Sufficient Condition|Sufficient Condition]] ===
0206 | 
0207 | Let:
0208 | :$(1)\quad$ For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $C \in \mathbf C : \alpha \tuple{C, -} : F \tuple{C, -} \to G \tuple{C, -}$ be a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
0209 | :$(2)\quad$ For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $D \in \mathbf D : \alpha \tuple{-, D} : F \tuple{-, D} \to G \tuple{-, D}$ be a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
0210 | 
0211 | By definition of [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]:
0212 | :for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $f: C \to C' \in \mathbf C$ and $g:D \to D' \in \mathbf D$:
0213 | ::$\map {G \tuple{-, D} } f \circ \alpha \tuple{-, D}_C = \alpha \tuple{-, D}_{C'} \circ \map {F \tuple{-, D} } f$
0214 | ::$\map {G \tuple{C, -} } g \circ \alpha \tuple{C, -}_D = \alpha \tuple{C, -}_{D'} \circ \map {F \tuple{C, -} } g$
0215 | 
0216 | That is 
0217 | :for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $f: C \to C' \in \mathbf C$ and $g:D \to D' \in \mathbf D$:
0218 | ::$(3)\quad \map G {f, \operatorname{id}_D} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } = \alpha_{\tuple{C', D} } \circ \map G {f, \operatorname{id}_D}$
0219 | ::$(4)\quad \map G {\operatorname{id}_C, g} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } = \alpha_{\tuple{C, D'} } \circ \map F {\operatorname{id}_C, g}$
0220 | by definitions of 
0221 | :* [[Definition:Functor|functors]] obtained by [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the first variable]] and [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the second variable]]
0222 | :* $\alpha \tuple{C, -}$ and $\alpha \tuple{-, D}$
0223 | 
0224 | For all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $\tuple{f: C \to C', g:D \to D'} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D$, we have:
0225 | {{begin-eqn}}
0226 | {{eqn | l = \map G {f, g} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} }
0227 |       | r = \map G {\operatorname{id}_{C'} \circ f, g \circ \operatorname{id}_D} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} }
0228 |       | c = {{Defof|Identity Morphism}}
0229 | }}
0230 | {{eqn | r = \map G {\tuple{\operatorname{id}_{C'}, g} \circ \tuple{f, \operatorname{id}_D} } \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} }
0231 |       | c = {{Defof|Product Category|Composition in Product Category}}
0232 | }}
0233 | {{eqn | r = \map G {\operatorname{id}_{C'}, g} \circ \map G {f, \operatorname{id}_D} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} }
0234 |       | c = {{Defof|Bifunctor}}
0235 | }}
0236 | {{eqn | r = \map G {\operatorname{id}_{C'}, g} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C', D} } \circ \map F {f, \operatorname{id}_D}
0237 |       | c = By $(3)$
0238 | }}
0239 | {{eqn | r = \alpha_{\tuple{C', D'} } \circ \map F {\operatorname{id}_{C'}, g} \circ \map F {f, \operatorname{id}_D}
0240 |       | c = By $(4)$
0241 | }}
0242 | {{eqn | r = \alpha_{\tuple{C', D'} } \circ \map F {\tuple{\operatorname{id}_{C'}, g} \circ \tuple{f, \operatorname{id}_{D} } }
0243 |       | c = {{Defof|Bifunctor}}
0244 | }}
0245 | {{eqn | r = \alpha_{\tuple{C', D'} } \circ \map F {\operatorname{id}_{C'} \circ f, g \circ  \operatorname{id}_{D} }
0246 |       | c = {{Defof|Product Category|Composition in Product Category}}
0247 | }}
0248 | {{eqn | r = \alpha_{\tuple{C', D'} } \circ \map F {f, g}
0249 |       | c = {{Defof|Identity Morphism}}
0250 | }}
0251 | {{end-eqn}}
0252 | 
0253 | It follows that $\alpha: F \to G$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]] by definition.{{qed}}
